stories.headline: Juniper Ridge wins both doubles and loses 5-2 to Westfield Friends
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Kevin Larue shook Levi Chesnut's hand at the net Wednesday after beating him 6-2, 7-5 at No. 4 singles. Chesnut had won his first 18 varsity matches, 16 of them as a freshman.

It was one of five singles matches Westfield Friends won at Juniper Ridge. Juniper Ridge's doubles pairs won both of theirs, and the defending 5A champions lost 5-2 at home to a 4A school from Fort Meriwether that is now 4-0.

Three of the five singles matches went to a third set. Deon Rennick took Maverick Kulp to a third-set tiebreak at second singles before losing 6-2, 2-6, 7-6, and Joshua Butcher lost 7-5, 3-6, 7-5 to Levi Bishop at third.
"They were better than us on Wednesday," Okafor said. "I'd rather find that out in August."
Grayson Adkins beat Ezekiel Amoore 7-6, 6-2 at the top of the order, two days after Amoore had come back from a set down at Liberty Hill.

Christian Pulliam and Gabriel Clark won 6-4, 4-6, 6-1 at No. 1 doubles, and freshman Dimitri Kimball and Gage McConathy won 6-2, 6-2 at No. 2. Juniper Ridge then opened the Kajaani League Thursday with a 6-1 win at Cedar Exchange, Amoore winning 6-1, 6-3.
Juniper Ridge (3-1, 1-0 Kajaani) hosts Lateral Seven Friday.

stories.headline: Carroway freshmen win at No. 1 doubles in a 4-3 loss
stories.byline: By Dale Kreuger | Courier staff writer
body: Four matches went to a third set at Carroway Thursday, and Jimmy Carter of Garrow won all four to win the dual 4-3.

Senior Michael Stevens took the first set 6-3 at fifth singles and lost the next two 7-6, 7-5 to sophomore Gabriel Fong. Freshman Leo Walton at third singles and junior James Stacy at fourth also lost in three, and so did the No. 2 doubles team of Max Callender and freshman John Qin.

Carroway's points came at the top. Luke Palm, playing first singles after a season spent almost entirely in doubles, beat Ryan Byram 6-0, 6-3, and Primitivo Delgado won 6-4, 6-4 at second singles. The third point belonged to two of Haverkamp's seven freshmen, Uwe Fiebich and Rashad McCloud, who won 6-4, 3-6, 7-5 at No. 1 doubles in their second varsity dual.
Carroway beat Pacersburg 7-0 the day before. It opens the Juniper League Friday at Ostrander Union.
"Every one of those went three sets," Haverkamp said, "and every one of them is a kid who'll be better for it by October."

stories.headline: Notebook: Calder wins its league opener in doubles
body: Calder. Beat Obama 4-3 Wednesday in the Fiesta Athletic Association opener while losing first and second singles. Calder won three of the four doubles matches, and senior Luis Atteberry supplied the fourth point at third singles, 6-0, 6-4. Calder hosts Liberty Hill Friday; Liberty Hill (2-2) lost its league opener 6-1 at Tidewater Catholic Thursday.

Fairgrounds. Freshman Damien Paquette has played first singles in all three of the team's duals. Against Las Colinas he lost the first set 6-0 to senior Alex Kunkel and won the next two 6-4, 6-3. Fairgrounds still lost 4-3 and is 2-1.

Senator Gray. Recovered from Monday's 7-0 loss to Altamonte with road wins at Bitterroot (6-1) and Ditch Fork (5-2). Cranston Diggins won his first singles match at Bitterroot 6-4, 5-7, 7-6 over Joshua Cater.
High Desert Christian. Beat Cornerstone Christian 4-3 Tuesday for its first dual win of the season and lost to Trinity Catholic by the same score a day later.
Mt Jacqueline. Won 4-3 at Copper Gap Tuesday, then lost 7-0 at Mabryville.
Copper Gap and Marlow County. Both won their league openers 6-1, Copper Gap over Aspen Hollow and Marlow County over Archbishop Quinlan.

stories.headline: Friday's league duals
body: Carroway is at Ostrander Union in the Juniper League, Juniper Ridge hosts Lateral Seven and Calder hosts Liberty Hill. Covenant is at Mission Terrace, Navrang hosts Box Canyon and Trout Lake hosts Seamus Town.
